findings.message:
`deletePalette` leaves the active tab on the wrong palette

The index is only corrected when it is past the end. `[auto, A, B]` on B, then delete A: index 2 is out of range, so the view jumps to auto-history and B is hidden. `[auto, A, B, C]` on B, then delete A: the view lands on C. Deleting the active last palette clamps to 0 without calling `restoreAutoHistorySelection()`, so `activeHistoryID` still holds the deleted chip's id. The PR says this is handled, and it is not.
Fix: capture the index before removal. If `active == index`, set 0 and call `restoreAutoHistorySelection()`. If `active > index`, set `active - 1`. The durable fix is to store the active selection by palette `id`.

`savePalette` does not select the new chip, so the next swap is not saved

Unlike `addCurrentToPalette`, `savePalette` never sets `activeHistoryID`. `swap()`'s palette branch (`Eyedroppers.swift:88-94`) then finds no match and returns after swapping the on-screen colors. The saved chip keeps its pre-swap orientation.
Fix: set `activeHistoryID = current.id` after the write.

Undo/redo on a named tab writes into auto-history and clears redo

Base `applyHistoryEntry` was a plain setter. This PR routes it through `applyEntry`, which calls `recordHistory()` whenever `activePaletteIndex != 0`. Undo and redo restore via `applyRestoredSnapshot` → `applyHistoryEntry`, so on a named tab `recordHistory()` calls `pushUndo()` (which clears `redoStack`) and prepends a duplicate of the restored entry.
Repro: on auto, delete a middle entry, switch to a named palette, press Undo. Auto-history now holds the entry twice, the undo stack has a spurious snapshot, and redo is gone.
Fix: keep restore paths on a pure setter, as in base. Only navigation and chip taps should record history.

`swap()` pushes an auto-history undo snapshot even when a named chip changes

The PR says this is gated on auto-history. It is not. Base also pushed unconditionally, so this is a claimed fix that was not made. On a named tab, Undo then reverts nothing: it jumps the colors to the auto head and leaves a no-op redo entry.
Fix: call `pushUndo()` only on the tab-0 path.

Delete on a named tab with a stale selection changes colors and writes history instead of deleting

Clicking a named tab only sets the index, so `activeHistoryID` keeps the auto chip's id. Pressing Delete then runs `deleteCurrentEntry`'s palette branch. `deleteChipFromPalette` removes nothing, but the code still applies the palette's first chip, and `recordHistory()` writes it into auto-history. The same path opens when the active chip is removed from its palette, because `deleteChipFromPalette` does not clear `activeHistoryID`.
Fix: have `deleteChipFromPalette` return whether it removed anything, and apply the next entry only if it did. Clear `activeHistoryID` when the removed id matches. Route tab selection through one Eyedroppers method that resets the selection.

"New palette" does nothing while the drawer is hidden

`.savePalette` is observed only by `PaletteTabBar`. That view exists only inside `ColorHistoryDrawer`, which is mounted only when `historyDrawerVisible` is true. The handler's "open the drawer" branch can therefore never run when it is needed.
Fix: observe `.savePalette` in `ContentView`, set `historyDrawerVisible = true`, and signal the tab bar (for example with an incrementing request token) to show the name field.

Export discards write errors and does not sanitize the filename

- `try? json.write` drops every error. The repo has no `NSAlert`, so the PR's "errors surface via NSAlert" is not implemented.
- The filename only lowercases and replaces spaces. A name containing `/`, `:` or `\` reaches `nameFieldStringValue` unchanged. Combined with the silent `try?`, a name like "Warm/Cool" can fail with no feedback. The exact NSSavePanel behavior is unverified.
Fix: use `do/catch` with `NSAlert(error:).runModal()`, and strip `/`, `:` and `\` from `fileName`.

The swap button rotates twice per click

The button action runs `onSwap(); angle -= 180`. `onSwap` routes through `AppDelegate.triggerSwap`, which posts `.triggerSwap`. The `.onReceive` added by this PR on the same view also runs `angle -= 180`. Each click turns the icon −360°, so it ends where it started.
Fix: remove `angle -= 180` from the button action.

Auto-history and palette reads decode the whole `palettes` blob repeatedly

Auto-history now lives at `palettes[0].pairs`, in the same blob as every named palette. The `autoHistory` getter and setter each decode the full array, and the setter re-encodes and writes it. A single pick therefore costs several full decodes and one encode on the main thread. Named palettes are uncapped, so the cost grows with all saved colors rather than the 20-entry history. In the drawer, `activePalette` is read inside the chip `ForEach`. If `Defaults` decodes on every read (the library is not in the workspace, so this is unverified), that adds one decode per chip. These are estimates, not measurements.
Fix: restore a separate capped `colorHistory` key for auto-history. Read `Defaults[.palettes]` once per operation, and hoist `activePalette` into a local in the drawer body.

The migration overwrites `palettes` instead of merging

The PR says legacy `colorHistory` is merged into `palettes[0].pairs`. The code assigns `Defaults[.palettes] = [history]`, which drops all named palettes and any existing auto pairs. A normal upgrade from base is safe because `palettes` still holds the default empty auto palette. Data loss needs `colorHistory` to be non-empty while `palettes` already has content, for example after a downgrade and re-upgrade.
Fix: merge into the existing auto palette (capped at `maxHistory`), and clear `colorHistory` only after the write succeeds.

Typing "h", "p" or "c" in the palette name field may trigger global toggles

`h` and `p` already existed. `c` is new in this PR. The key monitor returns events unchanged while a text field is first responder, so plain letters reach SwiftUI. Whether the hidden modifier-less `keyboardShortcut` buttons consume them before the text field is unverified and needs a manual check. If they do, typing "Cool" toggles compliance, and typing "h" closes the drawer and loses the name.
Fix: drop the modifier-less single-letter shortcuts, or gate them on the first responder not being a text view.

Compliance icon never changes shape

Both branches are `"checkmark.shield"`. `checkmark.shield.fill` appears nowhere, although the PR describes it.
Fix: `showCompliance ? "checkmark.shield.fill" : "checkmark.shield"`.

Named-palette chips show "Remove from history"

`ColorHistoryChip` always uses `textHistoryRemove`. `PikaText.textPaletteRemoveChip` (`Pika/Constants/Constants.swift:216`) is defined but used nowhere.
Fix: pass a `removeLabel` into the chip, chosen by `isAutoHistory`.

Rename state is keyed by array index

If another palette is deleted while the name field is open, `renamingIndex` now points at a different palette, and submitting renames the wrong one.
Fix: key rename state by `Palette.id`.

`Eyedroppers` now owns palette persistence, with repeated logic

`renamePalette`, `deletePalette`, `addCurrentToPalette` and `deleteChipFromPalette` each repeat the fetch, the `index > 0` guard and the write-back. The `ColorPair(...)` literal is repeated in `clearHistory`, `savePalette` and `addCurrentToPalette`.
Fix: add a `mutatePalette(at:_:)` helper. Longer term, extract a small palette store.

The auto-history rule is expressed in several ways

`Palette.isAutoHistory` (`name == nil`) and `ColorHistoryDrawer.isAutoHistory` (`activePaletteIndex == 0`) share a name but mean different things. Nothing ties name-nil to index 0.
Fix: use one predicate everywhere.

Alert buttons are hard-coded English

The title and message are localized through `PikaText`, but `"Clear"` and `"Cancel"` are literals.
Fix: add localized `PikaText` entries and use them.

The date formatter is still created per pair

The PR says `ISO8601DateFormatter` was hoisted out of the `map` closure. It was not.
Fix: hoist it, or correct the PR description.
